title: Fabric GEM flags the causal ANTXR2 variant, and clinicians diagnose infantile hyaline fibromatosis in an infant
summary: In rapid genome sequencing, Fabric GEM scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant at 4.7; clinicians diagnosed an infant within five days, and the result changed her care.
account: The case report dates the girl's abnormal neurological development to two months of age. It included bilateral upper-extremity hypotonia, a weak palmar grasp, pain with all passive and active extremity movement and bilateral contractures. A bleeding, ulcerated infantile hemangioma in the center of the neck was managed from three months of age. The diminishing appetite and abdominal distension were noted at four months. At four months she was referred to the pediatric emergency department at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital for failure to thrive with abdominal distension and global developmental delay. Rapid whole-genome sequencing at Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine used the Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence analysis tool with Phevor re-ranking. The sample was shipped on 5 January 2023, and preliminary results were returned on 10 January 2023. GEM scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant, c.652T>C (p.Cys218Arg), at 4.7. The clinicians diagnosed infantile hyaline fibromatosis syndrome from that finding. At a multidisciplinary meeting the same day, clinicians conveyed the implications, coordinated gastrostomy tube placement and discussed long-term goals. Treating clinicians reported the case in Cureus on 9 June 2024. The report's abstract describes her as a six-month-old infant with a history of painful extremity contractures. In October 2026 the treating team reported its three-year series of 52 rapid genome tests from four New Jersey centers, in which this infant is patient 1-31. The authors report that her result informed family planning, started disease-specific supportive care, changed her level of care and helped her move to palliative care because of the poor prognosis.
purpose: Rank candidate variants from rapid whole-genome sequencing against the patient's phenotype so that clinicians can reach a molecular diagnosis quickly.
system: Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence variant interpretation tool with Phevor phenotype-driven re-ranking
deployer: Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine and Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
location: New Brunswick, New Jersey, United States
segment: Critically ill infant undergoing rapid whole-genome sequencing

ratings.reason: An identifiable infant received a definitive molecular diagnosis of a disorder that the authors say frequently causes early death before age two. A multidisciplinary meeting the same day coordinated gastrostomy tube placement and long-term goals. The treating team's 2026 series reports that the result informed family planning, started disease-specific supportive care, changed her level of care and helped her move to palliative care because of the poor prognosis.

In this single case, preliminary results were returned on 10 January 2023, five days after the sample was shipped on 5 January 2023. Genomic panels and a microarray sent from the institution were still pending and were anticipated to take longer than one month. The report does not say what became of those tests.

ai_role.statement: GEM scored and surfaced the homozygous ANTXR2 variant at 4.7. The paper says Bayes factor scores greater than 2 are considered strong support. Phevor also identified the variant but scored it 1. That is below the Phevor score of 5 or above that the paper treats as further guidance on what to prioritize. The clinicians then confirmed and interpreted the finding and made the diagnosis. The report is written by the treating clinicians and a Rady clinical genomics scientist, not by the tool's vendor.

fields.summary: In rapid genome sequencing, Fabric GEM scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant at 4.7; clinicians diagnosed an infant within five days, and the result changed her care.
fields.account: The case report dates the girl's abnormal neurological development to two months of age. It included bilateral upper-extremity hypotonia, a weak palmar grasp, pain with all passive and active extremity movement and bilateral contractures. A bleeding, ulcerated infantile hemangioma in the center of the neck was managed from three months of age. The diminishing appetite and abdominal distension were noted at four months. At four months she was referred to the pediatric emergency department at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital for failure to thrive with abdominal distension and global developmental delay. Rapid whole-genome sequencing at Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine used the Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence analysis tool with Phevor re-ranking. The sample was shipped on 5 January 2023, and preliminary results were returned on 10 January 2023. GEM scored a homozygous ANTXR2 variant, c.652T>C (p.Cys218Arg), at 4.7. The clinicians diagnosed infantile hyaline fibromatosis syndrome from that finding. At a multidisciplinary meeting the same day, clinicians conveyed the implications, coordinated gastrostomy tube placement and discussed long-term goals. Treating clinicians reported the case in Cureus on 9 June 2024. The report's abstract describes her as a six-month-old infant with a history of painful extremity contractures. In October 2026 the treating team reported its three-year series of 52 rapid genome tests from four New Jersey centers, in which this infant is patient 1-31. The authors report that her result informed family planning, started disease-specific supportive care, changed her level of care and helped her move to palliative care because of the poor prognosis.
